coverage: Both complete English editions: named cast including final silent daughters, all speaker roles, named ancestors and divine references. Parentage is not explained before the play establishes it.

entities.name: Oedipus
entities.body: King of Thebes and husband of Jocasta.

snapshots.body: The king of Thebes, now revealed as the son of Laius and of his own wife, Jocasta.

entities.name: Jocasta
entities.body: Queen of Thebes, wife of Oedipus and sister of Creon. Formerly married to Laius.

snapshots.body: Oedipus’s wife and mother, formerly married to Laius; Creon’s sister.

entities.name: Creon
entities.body: Jocasta’s brother and an influential member of the Theban royal household.

entities.name: Teiresias
entities.body: The blind prophet consulted by Thebes.

entities.name: Laius
entities.body: The former king of Thebes and Jocasta’s previous husband.

snapshots.body: The former king of Thebes, husband of Jocasta and father of Oedipus.

entities.name: Polybus
entities.body: King of Corinth and Oedipus’s father.

snapshots.body: The king of Corinth who raised Oedipus as his son, though they were not related by blood.

entities.name: Merope
entities.body: Queen of Corinth, wife of Polybus and mother of Oedipus.

snapshots.body: Polybus’s wife, who raised Oedipus in Corinth as her son.

entities.name: The priest of Zeus
entities.body: The elderly priest speaking for the people gathered outside Oedipus’s palace.

entities.name: The Theban elders
entities.body: The elders of Thebes who speak and sing as the chorus.

entities.name: The Corinthian messenger
entities.body: The messenger bringing news from Corinth.

snapshots.body: The messenger from Corinth, a former shepherd who brought the infant Oedipus to Polybus.

entities.name: Laius’s herdsman
entities.body: The old shepherd who served King Laius.

entities.name: The palace messenger
entities.body: The servant reporting events inside the Theban palace.

entities.name: Antigone
entities.body: A daughter of Oedipus and Jocasta, and Ismene’s sister.

entities.name: Ismene
entities.body: A daughter of Oedipus and Jocasta, and Antigone’s sister.

entities.name: Menoeceus
entities.body: The father of Creon and Jocasta.

entities.name: Labdacus
entities.body: Laius’s father, an ancestor of the Theban royal line.

entities.name: Polydorus
entities.body: Cadmus’s son and Labdacus’s father in the Theban royal ancestry.

entities.name: Cadmus
entities.body: The legendary founder of Thebes.

entities.name: Agenor
entities.body: Cadmus’s father in the royal ancestry recited by Oedipus.

entities.name: The Sphinx
entities.body: The riddling monster that once threatened Thebes.

entities.name: Zeus
entities.body: The chief god of the Greek pantheon.

entities.name: Athena
entities.body: The Greek goddess of wisdom and protector of cities, also called Pallas.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: The god of prophecy whose oracle at Delphi guides the inquiry. Also called Phoebus and Loxias.

entities.name: Artemis
entities.body: The Greek goddess of the hunt, Apollo’s sister.

entities.name: Ares
entities.body: The Greek god of war, invoked here as a destructive power afflicting the city.

entities.name: Amphitrite
entities.body: The sea goddess, whose domain is invoked as a distant place of banishment.

entities.name: Pluto
entities.body: The ruler of the underworld, also known as Hades.

entities.name: Bacchus
entities.body: Dionysus, the god of wine and ecstatic worship, closely associated with Thebes.

entities.name: Pan
entities.body: The rustic god of shepherds and wild mountain places.

entities.name: Hermes
entities.body: The messenger god associated with Mount Cyllene.

entities.name: The Pythia
entities.body: The priestess who speaks Apollo’s oracle at Delphi.

entities.name: The Fates
entities.body: The divine powers governing destiny in Greek tradition.

entities.name: The Maenads
entities.body: The ecstatic female followers of Bacchus.
